html: The Holikachuk, who call themselves Doogh Hit'an, are an Athabaskan-speaking Alaska Native people of the middle and upper Innoko River in western Alaska. Their language stands between those of the Koyukon and the Deg Xit'an, and they took up many ways of their western neighbours, the Yup'ik. Their name comes from that of their old village on the Innoko. In 1963 the people moved to Grayling on the Yukon River. The Holikachuk language has almost died out.
